prompt:
Write 6 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a hit while turning left claim, in time order. Injury: neck and back strain. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1164; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment ran somewhat longer than usual for this injury.
- Years ago the patient had a small strain in the same area that healed fully.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- It is not clear whether all of the damage came from this impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: Claim received for a collision at an intersection where the insured's vehicle was turning left and was struck by an oncoming vehicle. The claimant reports neck and back strain and is not represented by an attorney. The driver is named on the policy, and the coverage was in force at the time of loss with no indication of earlier damage to the vehicle.

Entry 2: Police report and two independent witnesses confirm the accident occurred as described, and the other driver's statement matches. Photographs of the scene and both vehicles are on file. The claimant was confirmed to be in the vehicle at the time of the crash.

Entry 3: The claimant's account has stayed consistent across every conversation so far, including the initial call and the recorded interview. The reported injuries fit the type and force of the impact seen in the vehicle photos.

Entry 4: Medical records show a history of a minor strain in the same area several years ago, which resolved fully with no ongoing limitation. Treatment following this accident has run somewhat longer than is typical for this kind of injury, and the provider notes are being requested to review the course of care.

Entry 5: It is not yet clear how much of the current symptoms and damage stems from this impact versus the earlier strain or other factors. A records review and possibly an independent medical review will be needed to separate those contributions.

Entry 6: Nothing in the file suggests the damage predates the policy's effective date. Next step is to obtain the complete treatment records and the independent review results before setting a reserve and deciding on the bodily injury evaluation.
